Implementation Plan Implementation Plan — issue P2 of tracking #8427: Done-check (acceptance) behind `PERSIST_ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED` The plan to implement P2 is ready. It has no blockers and two warnings, listed at the end. **Planning ref:** `orchestrator/project-8427` @ `12c1aa23350f30261e9af6d8222e8ea0f2a446c5` (integration branch mismatch: false). **Spec:** the P2 parts of `docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md`: Phases & Merge Strategy item 2, Implementation Steps "P2: Done-check (acceptance)", decision D4, and the Tests section ("done-check parse and validate…"). The spec is present on this ref. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends partial_delivery._unfenced_lines Scope-mode justification: P2 is one bounded phase with a fixed list of deliverables in the spec. The deliverables are: - the plan fragment (template plus rendered copy); - `scripts/acceptance_check.py validate|marker|parse|render`; - a validation step in plan.yml; - the `AI_ACCEPTANCE_V1` marker in the plan comment; - the `## Acceptance` section in the implement PR body (status `not run`); - the heal `REPRODUCIBLE` derivation. This plan delivers all of them with nothing added from P3 or later phases. One small addition completes D4: the spec says the journal records `acceptance=invalid` with reasons. P1's `scripts/attempt_journal.py` already has an `acceptance` field (`ACCEPTANCE_STATES = ("met","unmet","invalid","none")`), but `cmd_append` always writes `{"state":"none"}`. A new `--acceptance-file` flag (about 10 lines) fills it, which is far cheaper than a separate journal path. By the Boil-the-Lake rule and §6 of `unattended_system_instructions.md` (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete option wins: it costs under 30 lines and adds no new dependency or external interface. Reuse is layered: - Layer 1: `partial_delivery._unfenced_lines`, `partial_delivery.HEAL_CF_LINE_RE`, `partial_delivery.sanitize_item`, `targeted_file_context.extract_paths_from_plan` and the P1 journal. - Layer 2: the `mode-plan-heal-counterfactual.txt` install and append pattern (plan.yml and `run_plan_codex.sh`), and the existing gate-summary append in implement's PR body. - Layer 3: the only net-new code is the `acceptance_check.py` grammar, validators and renderer, because nothing in the repo parses `ACCEPTANCE:` lines. ## Files likely to change - `prompts/_templates/mode-plan-acceptance.txt` (new) - `prompts/mode-plan-acceptance.txt` (new, byte-identical rendered copy) - `scripts/acceptance_check.py` (new) - `scripts/run_plan_codex.sh` (append only) - `scripts/attempt_journal.py` (additive flag) - `.github/workflows/plan.yml` - `.github/workflows/implement.yml` - `tests/test_acceptance_check.py` (new) - `tests/test_attempt_journal.py` - `agents.d/8427-p2-persist-acceptance.md` (new) - `changelog.d/8427-p2-persist-acceptance.md` (new) ## §20 Automation surface - **New or extended code:** one new library script, `scripts/acceptance_check.py`. Existing workflow steps call it; it is not a manual script. The other changes extend existing scripts and workflows. - **Entry points:** no new triggers. The existing triggers are reused: - `.github/workflows/plan.yml` (issue_comment `/answer`): a new step after "Parse planning output", plus an edit to "Post implementation plan". - `.github/workflows/implement.yml` (`/approved`, dispatch): the PR-body compose step just before "Create Pull Request". - **Long-running supervisor:** none. - **DB work:** none. No MongoDB collections or contracts are touched. - **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry. This is a permanent library step, as the spec's §18 table says. ## Functions or modules to implement **1. `prompts/_templates/mode-plan-acceptance.txt` and `prompts/mode-plan-acceptance.txt`** (byte-identical) - Header `# tier: DEFAULT`, then `=== DONE-CHECK (ACCEPTANCE) ===`, in the same style as `mode-plan-heal-counterfactual.txt`. - It tells the planner to add a `## Acceptance` section as its own `##` heading, after `## Files likely to change` and never inside it. The plan approval gate reads `.github/` tokens in the Files section only. - Lines are written unfenced, at the start of the line, not as bullets and not in backticks: - `ACCEPTANCE: test [::] [red-on-base]`: at most 10. `red-on-base` is required for bug fixes and regressions. - `ACCEPTANCE: check `: at most 5. - Exactly one of `ACCEPTANCE: post-merge workflow <.github/workflows/file.yml> [job ]` or `ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: `. - At least one `test` or `check` line. - Prefer tests the change adds or edits. Never name a test that needs network or credentials. - Heal plans that carry `HEAL_COUNTERFACTUAL: REPRODUCIBLE:` may omit the lines. - `mode-plan.txt` and the inline contract in `run_plan_codex.sh` stay unchanged, as spec step 2 requires. **2. `scripts/acceptance_check.py`** (tabs; `#!/usr/bin/env python3`; standard library only) - **Imports.** `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))` before importing `partial_delivery` and `targeted_file_context`, the same pattern as `attempt_journal.py:350`. This is needed because `python3 -I` does not add the script directory to the path. YAML is optional (`try: import yaml`) with a line-based fallback; PyYAML is absent in this sandbox and may be absent on runners. - **`parse_acceptance_lines(plan_text) -> (items, errors)`.** - Takes the `_unfenced_lines` after the first `## Files likely to change` heading (same `LIKELY_HEADER_RE` semantics) and matches `^ {0,3}ACCEPTANCE:[ \t]+(.*?)[ \t]*$`. - Grammar: - `test ((?:::)?)( red-on-base)?`. The path matches `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,300}`: no leading `/`, no `..` segment, no backslash. The name matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.\[\]:/-]{1,200}`. - `check `: 1–200 chars after control-character stripping; no backticks or `|`. - `post-merge workflow (\.github/workflows/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.ya?ml)( job )?`. - `post-merge none: `. - Anything else gives the error `unknown_form:`. - **`validate(plan_text, repo_root) -> dict`.** Builds `acceptance.v1`: `{"schema":"acceptance.v1","state":"valid|invalid|none","source":"plan|heal","tests":[{"path","name","red_on_base"}],"checks":[{"name"}],"post_merge":{"workflow","job"}|null,"post_merge_none":""|"","errors":[...]}`. - `state=none` when there are no `ACCEPTANCE:` lines and no heal derivation. - `state=invalid` when there is any error. Error codes: - `missing_test_path:

`: the file is not a regular non-symlink file under `repo_root`, and the path is not in `extract_paths_from_plan`; - `unknown_check:`; - `missing_workflow:`; - `unknown_job::`; - `too_many_tests` (more than 10) and `too_many_checks` (more than 5); - `no_test_or_check`; - `post_merge_count:` (when k ≠ 1, except for heal derivation); - `marker_too_large`. - Errors are capped at 20 entries of 200 chars each. - No network calls. - **`_workflow_jobs(repo_root) -> dict[file, {ids, names}]`.** - Reads only regular `.github/workflows/*.yml|*.yaml` files of 1 MB or less. - With yaml, it uses `jobs..name`. - Without yaml, it scans lines: the `jobs:` key at column 0, job ids at 2-space indent, and `name:` at 4-space indent under the current job id (quotes stripped). - A check name matches when it equals a job name or a job id (the id is used when no name is set). It also matches when the part before the first ` / ` equals one, which covers reusable-workflow check runs. Names containing `${{` never match. - **Heal derivation.** When no `ACCEPTANCE:` lines exist and an unfenced line matching `partial_delivery.HEAL_CF_LINE_RE` has the value `REPRODUCIBLE: ` (ids separated by commas or spaces): - each id becomes a `test red-on-base` item (same path validation); - `post_merge` is null and `source` is `heal`; no post-merge line is required; - otherwise heals follow the normal contract. - **`marker_line(obj) -> str`.** - Returns ``, with `<`, `>` and `&` replaced by `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026` (the P1 escaping precedent). - If the line is over 6000 bytes, `validate` turns the result `invalid` with `marker_too_large`. - **`parse_marker(comment_text) -> dict`.** Trailer position only: - Find the last line equal to ``. The line directly before it must match `^$`. - The JSON is re-normalised through the same validator for shape and charset, without file checks, and `state` must be `valid`. - Anything else returns `{"state":"none"}`. This defeats markers the model writes into its plan text, which always sit above the host trailer lines `/approved` and `/reclarify`. - **`render(obj, gate_result=None) -> str`.** Produces: - `## Acceptance`; - a one-line note that the done-check comes from the approved plan; - a `| Kind | Target | Status |` table; - a `Post-merge:` line (workflow/job, `none: `, or `not required (heal)`). Status is `not run` unless `gate_result["acceptance"]["items"]` has a matching `{kind,target,status}`, with status in `met|unmet|unmet (passes on base)|not run`. Values go through `partial_delivery.sanitize_item`, which neutralises `#N` and `@mention` and strips control characters. The renderer also removes backticks and escapes `|`. - **CLI (argparse subcommands).** Exit 0 on handled outcomes, non-zero only on usage or IO errors. Only tokens are logged: - `validate --plan-file --repo-root --out` prints `PERSIST acceptance outcome= errors=` to stderr. - `marker --in ` prints the marker line, but only when state is `valid`; otherwise it prints nothing and exits 0. - `parse --plan-comment-file [--out]` writes the JSON. - `render --in
